import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# GNRS conjecture

The GNRS conjecture (Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, 2004) states that every minor-closed
family of finite graphs, other than the family of all graphs, has $\ell_1$ embeddings with bounded
distortion: there is a constant $C$, depending only on the family, such that the shortest-path
(pseudo)metric of every graph in the family, with respect to every nonnegative edge-length
function, embeds into an $\ell_1$ space with distortion at most $C$.

Equivalently (Linial–London–Rabinovich, GNRS), the multi-commodity max-flow/min-cut gap of
graphs in such a family is uniformly bounded. Only the metric embedding formulation is stated
here. The exclusion of the family of all graphs is essential: bounded-degree expander graphs on
$n$ vertices require distortion $\Omega(\log n)$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, GNRS conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNRS_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [GNRS04] Gupta, A., Newman, I., Rabinovich, Y., Sinclair, A. (2004). "Cuts, trees and
  $\ell_1$-embeddings of graphs." *Combinatorica* 24 (2), pp. 233--269.
* [LS13] Lee, J. R., Sidiropoulos, A. (2013). "Pathwidth, trees, and random embeddings."
  *Combinatorica* 33 (3), pp. 349--374. [arXiv:0910.1409](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1409)
-/
open SimpleGraph
namespace GNRSConjecture
variable {V W X : Type*}

def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (A w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w w' => Disjoint (A w) (A w')) ∧
    ∀ ⦃w w'⦄, H.Adj w w' → ∃ u ∈ A w, ∃ v ∈ A w', G.Adj u v
blocks.docstring:
`IsMinor H G` means that the graph `H` is a *minor* of the graph `G`, i.e. `H` can be
obtained from `G` by deleting vertices, deleting edges and contracting edges.

We use the standard equivalent description by *branch sets*: there is a family `A` of pairwise
disjoint vertex sets `A w ⊆ V(G)`, indexed by the vertices `w` of `H`, each inducing a connected
(in particular nonempty) subgraph of `G`, such that whenever `w` and `w'` are adjacent in `H`
there is an edge of `G` between `A w` and `A w'`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Matroid.IsMinor (matroids, not graphs); SimpleGraph.Subgraph / `≤` (subgraphs only, no contraction); SimpleGraph.Copy / IsContained (subgraph containment, no contraction).
justification.name: GNRSConjecture.IsMinor
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib defines the graph-minor relation for SimpleGraph (only Matroid.IsMinor exists). Defined via the standard branch-set model: a partial map φ : V → Option W whose fibres are nonempty and induce connected subgraphs of G, such that every edge of H is realised by an edge of G between the corresponding branch sets. This is the textbook (Diestel) characterisation of 'H is obtained from a subgraph of G by contracting edges', up to isomorphism.

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.of_le {H G : SimpleGraph V} (h : H ≤ G) : IsMinor H G :=
  ⟨fun v => {v}, fun _ => Connected.of_subsingleton,
    fun _ _ hvw => Set.disjoint_singleton.mpr hvw,
    fun u v huv => ⟨u, rfl, v, rfl, h huv⟩⟩
blocks.docstring: Every subgraph of `G` (on the same vertex set) is a minor of `G`.

  ⟨fun v => {v}, fun _ => Connected.of_subsingleton,
    fun _ _ hvw => Set.disjoint_singleton.mpr hvw,
    fun u v huv => ⟨u, rfl, v, rfl, h huv⟩⟩

blocks.docstring:
A family of finite graphs, given by the sets `F n` of its members with vertex set `Fin n`,
is *minor-closed* if it contains every minor of each of its members.

Every finite graph is isomorphic to a graph on some `Fin n`, and since isomorphic graphs are
minors of each other, a minor-closed family is in particular closed under isomorphism.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No minor-closed graph-family predicate was found in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
justification.name: GNRSConjecture.IsMinorClosed
justification.why_needed: Minor closure must be expressed for a family whose finite graphs can have varying vertex cardinalities.

blocks.name: IsMinorClosed
blocks.text:
/-- A family of finite graphs, given by the sets `F n` of its members with vertex set `Fin n`,
is *minor-closed* if it contains every minor of each of its members.

Every finite graph is isomorphic to a graph on some `Fin n`, and since isomorphic graphs are
minors of each other, a minor-closed family is in particular closed under isomorphism. -/
def IsMinorClosed (F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃n m : ℕ⦄ ⦃G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)⦄ ⦃H : SimpleGraph (Fin m)⦄,
    G ∈ F n → IsMinor H G → H ∈ F m

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinorClosed_univ : IsMinorClosed fun _ => Set.univ :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => Set.mem_univ _
blocks.docstring: The family of all finite graphs is minor-closed.
blocks.name: isMinorClosed_univ
blocks.text:
/-- The family of all finite graphs is minor-closed. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinorClosed_univ : IsMinorClosed fun _ => Set.univ :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => Set.mem_univ _

noncomputable def shortestPathDist (G : SimpleGraph V) (w : Sym2 V → ℝ) (u v : V) : ℝ :=
  ⨅ p : G.Walk u v, (p.edges.map w).sum
blocks.docstring:
The shortest-path distance between `u` and `v` in the graph `G` with respect to the
edge-length function `w : Sym2 V → ℝ` (only the values of `w` on edges of `G` matter): the
infimum, over all walks `p` from `u` to `v` in `G`, of the total length of the edges of `p`.

For nonnegative `w` and connected `G` this is the shortest-path pseudometric $d_w$ *supported
on* `G`; it is only a pseudometric since zero-length edges are allowed. (For vertices in different
components the set of walks is empty and the infimum takes the junk value `0`, so the conjecture
below is stated for connected graphs.)

justification.name: GNRSConjecture.shortestPathDist
justification.why_needed: Shortest-path (pseudo)metric on the vertices of a graph with nonnegative real edge lengths: sInf of walkLength over all walks u → v. Mathlib's SimpleGraph.dist / edist are unweighted only.

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem shortestPathDist_nonneg (G : SimpleGraph V) {w : Sym2 V → ℝ} (hw : ∀ e, 0 ≤ w e)
    (u v : V) : 0 ≤ shortestPathDist G w u v :=
  Real.iInf_nonneg fun p => List.sum_nonneg fun x hx => by
    obtain ⟨e, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hx
    exact hw e

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem shortestPathDist_self (G : SimpleGraph V) {w : Sym2 V → ℝ} (hw : ∀ e, 0 ≤ w e)
    (u : V) : shortestPathDist G w u u = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (shortestPathDist_nonneg G hw u u)
  have hbdd : BddBelow (Set.range fun p : G.Walk u u => (p.edges.map w).sum) := by
    refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
    rintro x ⟨p, rfl⟩
    exact List.sum_nonneg fun x hx => by
      obtain ⟨e, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hx
      exact hw e
  simpa using ciInf_le hbdd (Walk.nil : G.Walk u u)

blocks.docstring:
A pseudometric `d` on `X` *embeds into `ℓ₁` with distortion at most `C`* if there are
`n : ℕ` and a map `f : X → ℝⁿ` such that, measuring distances in `ℝⁿ` with the `ℓ₁` (sum) norm,
$$d(x, y) \le \|f(x) - f(y)\|_1 \le C \cdot d(x, y)$$
for all `x y : X`.

This is the usual non-contracting normalisation: an embedding with
`c * d x y ≤ ‖f x - f y‖₁ ≤ C' * d x y` and stretch factor `C' / c ≤ C` can be rescaled to one of
the above form. For finite `X`, embeddings into the sequence space `ℓ₁` (or into `L₁`) can be
replaced by embeddings into some finite-dimensional `ℓ₁ⁿ` without changing the distortion.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's Bilipschitz file (only works with antilipschitzWith/LipschitzWith on metric-space instances, not on a pseudometric given as a function, and does not fix the ℓ₁ target); Isometry; lp (fun _ : ℕ => ℝ) 1 as target (equivalent for finite metrics; finite-dimensional PiLp 1 chosen as the notes suggest).
justification.name: GNRSConjecture.EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion
justification.why_needed: 'd embeds into ℓ₁ with distortion at most C': ∃ n and f : V → PiLp 1 (Fin n → ℝ) with d u v ≤ dist (f u) (f v) ≤ C * d u v. No Mathlib notion of metric distortion / bi-Lipschitz distortion into ℓ₁ exists in a usable form.

blocks.name: EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion
blocks.text:
/-- A pseudometric `d` on `X` *embeds into `ℓ₁` with distortion at most `C`* if there are
`n : ℕ` and a map `f : X → ℝⁿ` such that, measuring distances in `ℝⁿ` with the `ℓ₁` (sum) norm,
$$d(x, y) \le \|f(x) - f(y)\|_1 \le C \cdot d(x, y)$$
for all `x y : X`.

This is the usual non-contracting normalisation: an embedding with
`c * d x y ≤ ‖f x - f y‖₁ ≤ C' * d x y` and stretch factor `C' / c ≤ C` can be rescaled to one of
the above form. For finite `X`, embeddings into the sequence space `ℓ₁` (or into `L₁`) can be
replaced by embeddings into some finite-dimensional `ℓ₁ⁿ` without changing the distortion. -/
def EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion (d : X → X → ℝ) (C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : X → PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)),
    ∀ x y, d x y ≤ dist (f x) (f y) ∧ dist (f x) (f y) ≤ C * d x y

@[category test, AMS 46]
theorem embedsIntoL1WithDistortion_real :
    EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion (fun x y : ℝ => |x - y|) 1 := by
  refine ⟨1, fun x => WithLp.toLp 1 (fun _ => x), fun x y => ?_⟩
  simp [PiLp.dist_eq_sum, Real.dist_eq]

theorem gnrs_conjecture (F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) (hF : IsMinorClosed F)
    (hF' : ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∉ F n) :

blocks.docstring:
**The GNRS conjecture** (Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, 2004).

Let $\mathcal F$ be a minor-closed family of finite graphs other than the family of all graphs
(equivalently, $\mathcal F$ forbids some minor). Then there is a constant $C = C(\mathcal F)$ such
that for every (connected) graph $G \in \mathcal F$ and every nonnegative edge-length function
$w$ on $G$, the shortest-path pseudometric $d_w$ on the vertices of $G$ embeds into $\ell_1$ with
distortion at most $C$; that is, there is a map $f$ from the vertices of $G$ into an $\ell_1$ space
with $d_w(u, v) \le \|f(u) - f(v)\|_1 \le C \cdot d_w(u, v)$ for all vertices $u, v$.

The constant $C$ depends only on the family $\mathcal F$, not on the individual graph or on the
edge lengths. Here a family of finite graphs is given by the sets `F n` of its members with vertex
set `Fin n`. The conclusion is only asserted for connected members of the family, since the
shortest-path metric of a disconnected graph takes infinite values; this loses nothing, as the
connected components of members of a minor-closed family belong to the family.
blocks.name: gnrs_conjecture

/--
**The GNRS conjecture** (Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, 2004).

Let $\mathcal F$ be a minor-closed family of finite graphs other than the family of all graphs
(equivalently, $\mathcal F$ forbids some minor). Then there is a constant $C = C(\mathcal F)$ such
that for every (connected) graph $G \in \mathcal F$ and every nonnegative edge-length function
$w$ on $G$, the shortest-path pseudometric $d_w$ on the vertices of $G$ embeds into $\ell_1$ with
distortion at most $C$; that is, there is a map $f$ from the vertices of $G$ into an $\ell_1$ space
with $d_w(u, v) \le \|f(u) - f(v)\|_1 \le C \cdot d_w(u, v)$ for all vertices $u, v$.

The constant $C$ depends only on the family $\mathcal F$, not on the individual graph or on the
edge lengths. Here a family of finite graphs is given by the sets `F n` of its members with vertex
set `Fin n`. The conclusion is only asserted for connected members of the family, since the
shortest-path metric of a disconnected graph takes infinite values; this loses nothing, as the
connected components of members of a minor-closed family belong to the family.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 46 68]
theorem gnrs_conjecture (F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) (hF : IsMinorClosed F)
    (hF' : ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∉ F n) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (n : ℕ), ∀ G ∈ F n, G.Connected →
      ∀ w : Sym2 (Fin n) → ℝ, (∀ e, 0 ≤ w e) →
        EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion (shortestPathDist G w) C := by
  sorry
end GNRSConjecture

claims.decomposer_note: Precise form (article/Lee–Sidiropoulos): for every minor-closed family F of finite graphs other than the family of all graphs (equivalently, F forbids some minor), there is a constant C = C(F) such that for every graph G in F and every nonnegative edge-length function, the induced shortest-path (pseudo)metric on V(G) embeds into ℓ₁ (finite-dimensional ℝ^n with the sum norm suffices) with distortion ≤ C; the constant depends on F but not on the individual graph or weights, the 'all graphs' exclusion is essential (expanders force Θ(log n) distortion), and the article's flow-cut-gap phrasing and the planar special case are only an equivalent rephrasing and an illustrative consequence, not separate questions posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates are faithful encodings of the same statement (proper minor-closed family of finite graphs ⇒ ∃ C uniform over graphs and nonnegative edge lengths such that the shortest-path pseudometric embeds into finite-dimensional ℓ₁ with d ≤ ‖f u − f v‖₁ ≤ C·d), and all compile cleanly. c06 was chosen as the base for the clearest shape: family as `∀ n, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))`, explicit `IsMinorClosed`, `∃ n G, G ∉ F n` for 'not all graphs', C quantified before graph and weights, `PiLp 1` target with Mathlib's `dist`, restriction to connected members with a docstring explaining why nothing is lost. Edits: replaced c06's Option-map minor definition by the paper-verbatim branch-set definition (from c03/c05, `Connected` forcing nonempty branch sets, `Pairwise Disjoint`), and added API/test lemmas for the bespoke definitions adapted from c02/c03/c06 (`IsMinor.of_le`, `IsMinor.refl`, empty/one-vertex minors, `isMinorClosed_univ`, `shortestPathDist_nonneg/_self`, real line isometric into ℓ₁). AMS 5 46 68.

context: In theoretical computer science and metric geometry, the GNRS conjecture connects the theory of graph minors, the stretch factor of embeddings, and the approximation ratio of multi-commodity flow problems. It is named after Anupam Gupta, Ilan Newman, Yuri Rabinovich, and Alistair Sinclair, who formulated it in 2004.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# GNRS conjecture

The GNRS conjecture (Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, 2004) states that every minor-closed
family of finite graphs, other than the family of all graphs, has $\ell_1$ embeddings with bounded
distortion: there is a constant $C$, depending only on the family, such that the shortest-path
(pseudo)metric of every graph in the family, with respect to every nonnegative edge-length
function, embeds into an $\ell_1$ space with distortion at most $C$.

Equivalently (Linial–London–Rabinovich, GNRS), the multi-commodity max-flow/min-cut gap of
graphs in such a family is uniformly bounded. Only the metric embedding formulation is stated
here. The exclusion of the family of all graphs is essential: bounded-degree expander graphs on
$n$ vertices require distortion $\Omega(\log n)$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, GNRS conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNRS_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [GNRS04] Gupta, A., Newman, I., Rabinovich, Y., Sinclair, A. (2004). "Cuts, trees and
  $\ell_1$-embeddings of graphs." *Combinatorica* 24 (2), pp. 233--269.
* [LS13] Lee, J. R., Sidiropoulos, A. (2013). "Pathwidth, trees, and random embeddings."
  *Combinatorica* 33 (3), pp. 349--374. [arXiv:0910.1409](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1409)
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace GNRSConjecture

variable {V W X : Type*}

/-- `IsMinor H G` means that the graph `H` is a *minor* of the graph `G`, i.e. `H` can be
obtained from `G` by deleting vertices, deleting edges and contracting edges.

We use the standard equivalent description by *branch sets*: there is a family `A` of pairwise
disjoint vertex sets `A w ⊆ V(G)`, indexed by the vertices `w` of `H`, each inducing a connected
(in particular nonempty) subgraph of `G`, such that whenever `w` and `w'` are adjacent in `H`
there is an edge of `G` between `A w` and `A w'`. -/
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (A w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w w' => Disjoint (A w) (A w')) ∧
    ∀ ⦃w w'⦄, H.Adj w w' → ∃ u ∈ A w, ∃ v ∈ A w', G.Adj u v

/-- Every subgraph of `G` (on the same vertex set) is a minor of `G`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.of_le {H G : SimpleGraph V} (h : H ≤ G) : IsMinor H G :=
  ⟨fun v => {v}, fun _ => Connected.of_subsingleton,
    fun _ _ hvw => Set.disjoint_singleton.mpr hvw,
    fun u v huv => ⟨u, rfl, v, rfl, h huv⟩⟩

/-- Every graph is a minor of itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsMinor.refl (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor G G := .of_le le_rfl

/-- The graph with no vertices is a minor of every graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_bot_empty (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsMinor (⊥ : SimpleGraph Empty) G :=
  ⟨Empty.elim, fun w => w.elim, fun w => w.elim, fun w => w.elim⟩

/-- The one-vertex graph is a minor of every connected graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinor_bot_unit (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : G.Connected) :
    IsMinor (⊥ : SimpleGraph Unit) G :=
  ⟨fun _ => Set.univ, fun _ => (induceUnivIso G).connected_iff.mpr hG,
    fun a b hab => absurd (Subsingleton.elim a b) hab,
    fun _ _ hab => absurd hab (by simp)⟩

/-- A family of finite graphs, given by the sets `F n` of its members with vertex set `Fin n`,
is *minor-closed* if it contains every minor of each of its members.

Every finite graph is isomorphic to a graph on some `Fin n`, and since isomorphic graphs are
minors of each other, a minor-closed family is in particular closed under isomorphism. -/
def IsMinorClosed (F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃n m : ℕ⦄ ⦃G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)⦄ ⦃H : SimpleGraph (Fin m)⦄,
    G ∈ F n → IsMinor H G → H ∈ F m

/-- The family of all finite graphs is minor-closed. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isMinorClosed_univ : IsMinorClosed fun _ => Set.univ :=
  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ => Set.mem_univ _

/-- The shortest-path distance between `u` and `v` in the graph `G` with respect to the
edge-length function `w : Sym2 V → ℝ` (only the values of `w` on edges of `G` matter): the
infimum, over all walks `p` from `u` to `v` in `G`, of the total length of the edges of `p`.

For nonnegative `w` and connected `G` this is the shortest-path pseudometric $d_w$ *supported
on* `G`; it is only a pseudometric since zero-length edges are allowed. (For vertices in different
components the set of walks is empty and the infimum takes the junk value `0`, so the conjecture
below is stated for connected graphs.) -/
noncomputable def shortestPathDist (G : SimpleGraph V) (w : Sym2 V → ℝ) (u v : V) : ℝ :=
  ⨅ p : G.Walk u v, (p.edges.map w).sum

/-- The shortest-path distance is nonnegative for nonnegative edge lengths. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem shortestPathDist_nonneg (G : SimpleGraph V) {w : Sym2 V → ℝ} (hw : ∀ e, 0 ≤ w e)
    (u v : V) : 0 ≤ shortestPathDist G w u v :=
  Real.iInf_nonneg fun p => List.sum_nonneg fun x hx => by
    obtain ⟨e, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hx
    exact hw e

/-- The shortest-path distance from a vertex to itself is `0` for nonnegative edge lengths. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem shortestPathDist_self (G : SimpleGraph V) {w : Sym2 V → ℝ} (hw : ∀ e, 0 ≤ w e)
    (u : V) : shortestPathDist G w u u = 0 := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ (shortestPathDist_nonneg G hw u u)
  have hbdd : BddBelow (Set.range fun p : G.Walk u u => (p.edges.map w).sum) := by
    refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
    rintro x ⟨p, rfl⟩
    exact List.sum_nonneg fun x hx => by
      obtain ⟨e, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 hx
      exact hw e
  simpa using ciInf_le hbdd (Walk.nil : G.Walk u u)

/-- A pseudometric `d` on `X` *embeds into `ℓ₁` with distortion at most `C`* if there are
`n : ℕ` and a map `f : X → ℝⁿ` such that, measuring distances in `ℝⁿ` with the `ℓ₁` (sum) norm,
$$d(x, y) \le \|f(x) - f(y)\|_1 \le C \cdot d(x, y)$$
for all `x y : X`.

This is the usual non-contracting normalisation: an embedding with
`c * d x y ≤ ‖f x - f y‖₁ ≤ C' * d x y` and stretch factor `C' / c ≤ C` can be rescaled to one of
the above form. For finite `X`, embeddings into the sequence space `ℓ₁` (or into `L₁`) can be
replaced by embeddings into some finite-dimensional `ℓ₁ⁿ` without changing the distortion. -/
def EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion (d : X → X → ℝ) (C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : X → PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)),
    ∀ x y, d x y ≤ dist (f x) (f y) ∧ dist (f x) (f y) ≤ C * d x y

/-- The real line embeds isometrically into `ℓ₁`. -/
@[category test, AMS 46]
theorem embedsIntoL1WithDistortion_real :
    EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion (fun x y : ℝ => |x - y|) 1 := by
  refine ⟨1, fun x => WithLp.toLp 1 (fun _ => x), fun x y => ?_⟩
  simp [PiLp.dist_eq_sum, Real.dist_eq]

/--
**The GNRS conjecture** (Gupta, Newman, Rabinovich and Sinclair, 2004).

Let $\mathcal F$ be a minor-closed family of finite graphs other than the family of all graphs
(equivalently, $\mathcal F$ forbids some minor). Then there is a constant $C = C(\mathcal F)$ such
that for every (connected) graph $G \in \mathcal F$ and every nonnegative edge-length function
$w$ on $G$, the shortest-path pseudometric $d_w$ on the vertices of $G$ embeds into $\ell_1$ with
distortion at most $C$; that is, there is a map $f$ from the vertices of $G$ into an $\ell_1$ space
with $d_w(u, v) \le \|f(u) - f(v)\|_1 \le C \cdot d_w(u, v)$ for all vertices $u, v$.

The constant $C$ depends only on the family $\mathcal F$, not on the individual graph or on the
edge lengths. Here a family of finite graphs is given by the sets `F n` of its members with vertex
set `Fin n`. The conclusion is only asserted for connected members of the family, since the
shortest-path metric of a disconnected graph takes infinite values; this loses nothing, as the
connected components of members of a minor-closed family belong to the family.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 46 68]
theorem gnrs_conjecture (F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))) (hF : IsMinorClosed F)
    (hF' : ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∉ F n) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (n : ℕ), ∀ G ∈ F n, G.Connected →
      ∀ w : Sym2 (Fin n) → ℝ, (∀ e, 0 ≤ w e) →
        EmbedsIntoL1WithDistortion (shortestPathDist G w) C := by
  sorry

end GNRSConjecture

items: The list-page entry is a noun phrase ('The GNRS conjecture on whether ...'), not a question, so the conjecture is stated as a positive assertion (theorem with `sorry`), not with `answer(sorry)`. The precise formulation follows the Wikipedia article and Lee–Sidiropoulos (arXiv:0910.1409, Conjecture 1.2 / definition of c₁).

A family of finite graphs is represented as `F : ∀ n : ℕ, Set (SimpleGraph (Fin n))` (the members with vertex set `Fin n`). Every finite graph is isomorphic to one on `Fin n`, and minor-closedness (with the bespoke `IsMinor`, which covers isomorphic copies) forces closure under isomorphism, so nothing is lost.
'Other than the family of all graphs' is formalised as `∃ n (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G ∉ F n`. For a minor-closed family this is equivalent to the paper's 'F forbids some minor'.

Minor relation defined by the branch-set model (partial map with nonempty connected fibres, each H-edge realised by a G-edge between the fibres). This is the standard characterisation of 'obtained from a subgraph by edge contractions', up to isomorphism; extra G-edges between branch sets are allowed (they correspond to deleted edges).

The conclusion is asserted only for connected members `G` of `F` (hypothesis `G.Connected`). For disconnected graphs the shortest-path metric takes infinite values and ℓ₁-distortion is meaningless; moreover `shortestPathDist` uses `sInf` over ℝ and would return the junk value 0 for vertices in different components. Since the components of members of a minor-closed family are themselves members, restricting to connected graphs loses nothing.

Edge lengths are `w : Sym2 V → ℝ` with `∀ e, 0 ≤ w e` (nonnegativity required on all of Sym2 V, not just on edges; equivalent since only edge values enter the walk lengths and any nonnegative function on edges extends by 0). Zero lengths are allowed, so the induced distance is a pseudometric, as in the paper.

Shortest-path distance is `sInf` over all walks (not just paths) of the walk length; for nonnegative weights and connected G the set is nonempty and bounded below by 0, so `sInf` is the genuine infimum, attained by a shortest path.
Distortion ≤ C is formalised in the normalised form d(u,v) ≤ ‖f u − f v‖₁ ≤ C·d(u,v) (as in Lee–Sidiropoulos), which is equivalent to Wikipedia's '[c·d, C·d] with distortion C/c' by rescaling f.

The ℓ₁ target is finite-dimensional `PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)` with n existentially quantified, as suggested in the decomposition notes; this is equivalent to embedding into ℓ₁ or L₁ for finite (pseudo)metrics (finite ℓ₁-metrics are finite nonnegative combinations of cut metrics).

C is quantified before the graph and the weights (constant depends only on the family). C is not required to be ≥ 1 or > 0; any C witnessing the inequalities for a graph with a pair at positive distance is automatically ≥ 1, and the statement is not trivialised for degenerate families (e.g. empty F gives a vacuous conclusion, as it mathematically should).
AMS tags 5 (combinatorics) and 46 (functional analysis; metric embeddings into Banach spaces).

reviewer_notes: The list entry is a terse noun phrase; the precise content was taken from the Wikipedia article and Lee–Sidiropoulos Conjecture 1.1 (for minor-closed F, 'forbids some minor' ⇔ 'F ≠ all graphs'). Stated as a plain assertion (7/8 candidates) rather than c04's `answer(sorry) ↔`, since the GNRS conjecture is itself the positive assertion; c04's form was not wrong. Modeling choices verified: (1) restricting to connected members (c02,c03,c05,c06,c07) and requiring inequalities only on reachable pairs (c01,c04,c08) are equivalent — components of a member of a minor-closed family are members, and an embedding on reachable pairs imposes no cross-component constraint; (2) `∀ e, 0 ≤ w e` on all of Sym2 V is equivalent to nonnegativity on edges since only edge values enter walk lengths; (3) infimum over walks equals shortest-path length for nonnegative weights on connected graphs (nonempty, bounded below by 0); (4) finite-dimensional ℓ₁ⁿ with n existential suffices for finite pseudometrics; (5) normalisation d ≤ ‖·‖₁ ≤ C·d is equivalent to the [cd, C'd] stretch-factor definition by rescaling; (6) extra `1 ≤ C` / `0 < C` (c01,c04,c07,c08) is harmless and was not included. Checked `PiLp 1` `dist` equals the coordinate sum of absolute differences and that `(G.induce s).Connected` forces `s` nonempty. Only the forward direction (the conjecture) is stated; the converse (all graphs have unbounded distortion) is a known theorem and mentioned only in the docstring. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
